key_insight: A two-phase causal discovery and time-series clustering analysis reveals that weld signal morphology in resistance spot welding is driven mainly by material alloying, sheet thickness, and electrode tip size rather than by faying-surface count.
engineering_relevance: The results provide physically interpretable process levers for improving weld monitoring and quality control across heterogeneous automotive stack-up configurations.
method: Causal discovery to separate structural drivers from correlated process effects
Analysis of a dataset drawn from over 1.8 million welds
evidence_signal: The study analyzes 15,096 representative profiles extracted from more than 1.8 million welds, linking process variables to resistance, displacement, and force signal morphology.
watch_item: Because the approach is data-driven and applied across multicollinear stack-ups, deployment should be checked carefully for domain shift across new materials, coatings, and gun setups.
paper_title: Causal discovery of signal morphology drivers in steel resistance spot welding: a high-dimensional data analysis
